page: Amazon Web Services x8i.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache, along with hardware support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets.

The system is equipped with 128 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a generous 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features no local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent workloads rely on remote block storage or networked volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs present.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution, supported by strong gzip compression throughput of 34.38 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 2171.0. Text processing performance reaches the top 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core computational throughput aligns with midrange baselines, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 15616.6 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8429.0. While small-model LLM generation runs efficiently at 304.11 tokens/sec, medium-model inference drops significantly to 8.63 tokens/sec, underscoring CPU execution limits for larger machine learning pipelines.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x8i.2xlarge prioritizes memory capacity and caching over raw parallel compute density. It offers an efficient profile for memory-bound systems that do not require high core counts. The instance is best suited for in-memory caching solutions like Redis, mid-sized relational database servers, enterprise in-memory analytics, and text-processing workflows that benefit from dense DDR5 memory and large L3 cache allocations.
